name: Berechiah
overview: Berechiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah known primarily as the son of Meshullam. His brief biblical mention situates him within the genealogical records of Israel, specifically in 1 Chronicles 3:20. Beyond this, Scripture provides no additional details about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Berechiah means 'YHWH blesses,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names that acknowledge God's favor. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:20 and was not given directly by God but carries a significant spiritual connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Berechiah as the son of Meshullam, establishing a direct father-son relationship. No other family connections or descendants are recorded in the biblical text beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Berechiah's significance lies in his inclusion within the genealogical lineage of Judah, which underscores the continuity of God's covenant people. Although his individual story is not detailed, his mention preserves the integrity of the biblical record and highlights the faithfulness of God's promises through generations.
